scope: S5 Tool broker lifecycle on exclusive disposable PostgreSQL and MinIO. The fixture adapter is a declared external-effect test seam; it is not a Workspace service, protected sandbox, Firecracker, or Linux/KVM execution claim.

observations.admission: Broker.Admit created the policy-bound pending approval; the owner-only public StateRuntime decision created the one-use grant before worker dispatch.
observations.durability: The worker finalized exactly one operation, persisted an owner-readable MinIO Artifact, and a new PostgreSQL pool plus StateRuntime replayed the terminal public Tool projection without a second adapter execution.
observations.authorization: An expired second brokered approval made no execution intent and no adapter call; the durable audit included capability_grant.expired.
observations.audit_and_output: Durable audit contained decision, grant-consumption, execution-intent, terminal-outcome, and grant-exhaustion phases. The artifact read through the owner-authorized public route retained a redacted bounded result and not the fixture credential-shaped value.
observations.limits: This proof demonstrates retained output redaction and the successful bounded artifact path only. The oversized-output durable rejection and uncertainty-recovery paths remain unclaimed.

redaction: No DSNs, object-store credentials, raw operation IDs, raw descriptors, raw input, artifact body, or backend endpoints are retained.
